newsitem.title: SPAIN: Telefonica shares not seen dulled by S&P news.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica shares not seen dulled by S&P news.

text.p: Shares in Telefonica de Espana are not seen negatively affected by a downgrade in its outlook rating given by Standard & Poor's earlier today, analysts said on Wednesday.

S&P said it had changed its outlook for the Spanish operator to "negative" from "stable," on the basis of its debt coverage levels and prospects for increased competition in the sector. However it confirmed its long-term "AA-" debt rating.
At 1415 GMT, Telefonica was down 10 pesetas, 0.23 percent, to 4,265 off a high of 4,345 pesetas before the news, while the Ibex-35 blue chip index was up 0.83 percent to 6,568.59.

"I don't think this should affect the shares very much as foreseeable prospects after liberalisation and the effects of its debt levels and the risk involve on further entry into international markets are already taken into account in valuations of the company," said Alberto Arroyo, analyst at BBV Interactivos brokerage.
Interactivos' year-end target price is 4,800 pesetas.
An analyst at another Spanish bank agreed.

"The outlook downgrade seems to be saying that S&P will be following Telefonica's progress carefully in terms of how it's doing with all the new investment involved in the BT -MCI deal, aimed at Latin America where there is much potential, but obviously more risk," said Javier Borrachero, analyst at Central Hispano Bolsa.
"But all of that is well-known, and fully discounted," he added.

However Borrachero added that although prospects for Telefonica medium term are positive, short-term he expects the shares to trade in line with the market as all the good news has already been taken into account.
